gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 7?

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Official forecasts from the National Weather Service place the August 7 high near 91°F under a heat advisory, with mostly sunny skies and a 20% chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms.** This consensus anchors trader sentiment around the 88–93°F brackets, where the three leading outcomes capture model-to-model differences in boundary-layer heating and convective timing. Southwest flow advects warm, moist air while strong insolation supports rapid temperature rises, but any earlier-than-expected cloud cover or storms can limit peak readings by 2–4°F through reduced solar input and evaporative cooling. Ensemble spreads and recent high-resolution guidance show minor disagreements on exact convective initiation after 2 p.m., keeping the 90–91°F outcome narrowly favored yet closely contested by the adjacent 88–89°F and 92–93°F bins. Historical August normals near 83°F underscore the anomalous warmth, but the market reflects the narrow uncertainty range typical for a one-day temperature resolution.

Traders are monitoring the next JMA update and real-time observations for any late-day adjustments before resolution.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from German Weather Service models and ensembles indicate Munich's August 7 maximum will likely peak near 27–28°C under high-pressure conditions with ample sunshine and light winds promoting daytime heating, directly supporting the tight market split between those two outcomes. Minor model disagreements on afternoon cloud development or boundary-layer mixing explain the close 43% versus 37.5% trader weighting, while probabilities drop sharply for 29°C or higher because current guidance shows insufficient instability for further warming. Historical August averages near 23–25°C provide context, yet this event's stable synoptic pattern has elevated expectations without crossing into heatwave thresholds. Updated model runs and official observations later today remain the key near-term catalysts for any probability shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**High pressure over the UK is driving a settled, sunny spell that favors peak temperatures in the low 30s Celsius for London on August 9.** 

Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble forecasts highlight an anticyclonic pattern with light southerly or variable winds advecting warmer air from the continent, combined with clear skies that maximize solar insolation during the longest day hours. This setup follows early-August heatwave conditions that already pushed southern England into the mid-30s, leaving residual warmth in the boundary layer. 

Model consensus points to a maximum near 31–32 °C at official sites (e.g., Heathrow or St James’s Park), where the urban heat-island effect can add 1–2 °C relative to rural surroundings. Small differences among 30 °C, 31 °C, and 32 °C outcomes hinge on subtle variables: exact cloud timing, boundary-layer mixing depth, and whether any weak Atlantic front arrives marginally earlier than currently modeled. These factors produce the tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around the 30–32 °C band, with traders weighting the latest high-resolution runs that keep the warmest air over southeast England through the afternoon of the 9th.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official National Weather Service forecasts for New York City on August 7, 2026, call for a high near 88°F under mostly sunny skies, with a 30% chance of showers and thunderstorms developing mainly after 2 p.m. and heat indices reaching 98°F.** This baseline supports the market’s leading buckets around 90–93°F, as traders weigh the potential for slightly warmer readings driven by urban heat island effects in Manhattan, reduced cloud cover early in the day, or stronger southerly flow ahead of any convection.

Key differentiating factors include the timing and intensity of afternoon thunderstorms, which could cap the peak if they initiate earlier than modeled, versus sustained clear conditions that allow full solar heating. Model consensus from NWS and others shows modest spread in maximum temperatures, with historical August variability around the 83°F average high providing context for why 88–93°F outcomes cluster tightly in trader pricing. Upcoming updates from NWS forecast discussions and real-time observations will likely refine these probabilities as the day progresses.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts for Tokyo on August 8 project a maximum near 32–34°C under partly to mostly cloudy conditions, aligning with the market's heaviest positioning on those outcomes. A strong subtropical high-pressure system continues to dominate, advecting warm, moist air northward, though increased cloud cover and potential scattered showers may limit peak heating compared with July's extreme "kokushobi" episodes that exceeded 40°C in parts of the Kanto region. Urban heat-island effects in central Tokyo typically add 1–2°C to official readings, while climatological normals for early August hover around 31–32°C. This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service outlooks and ensemble model guidance indicate a persistent warm, humid air mass over the Northeast, supported by high pressure and southerly flow, positioning NYC for an August 8 high most likely in the upper 80s to low 90s°F—well above the 83°F climatological average. This setup has driven the market’s heavy weighting toward 90-91°F (41.5%) and 88-89°F (30.5%), reflecting limited cooling from any overnight showers or modest cloud cover. Updated runs from the past 48 hours show minimal spread across guidance, with only low-probability scenarios for 92°F+ if mixing is stronger than expected. Final NHC and local office briefings tomorrow morning will provide the last model adjustments before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Japan Meteorological Agency show mostly cloudy skies over Tokyo on August 9 with daytime maxima centered near 32–34°C, reflecting typical mid-August conditions under a persistent subtropical high-pressure system that promotes hot, humid air advection from the Pacific. Ensemble guidance exhibits modest spread due to variable cloud cover and scattered shower potential, which can suppress peak readings by 1–2°C through reduced insolation while urban heat-island effects in central Tokyo sustain nighttime minima near 25°C and elevate daytime values. Traders appear to weigh these factors evenly between 32°C and 33°C outcomes, consistent with historical August averages around 31°C and the narrow window before resolution. Updated model runs and JMA briefings in the next 48 hours will likely refine probabilities as steering patterns and moisture fields evolve.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Market-implied odds cluster around 32–33°C** for Tokyo’s peak temperature on August 9, reflecting trader assessment of a near-normal summer day under mostly cloudy conditions rather than an extreme heat spike. 

Japan Meteorological Agency guidance issued August 7 projects mostly cloudy skies with 40–50% chance of scattered showers, which limits daytime insolation and caps maximum temperatures near the long-term August 9 average of roughly 31–32°C at the official Tokyo station. Persistent regional heat (above-normal temperatures signaled for central Japan) and typical urban heat-island amplification keep the upper tail (34°C+) in play if breaks of sun develop or warm advection strengthens, while higher humidity and light winds could nudge the reading toward the lower side of the 32–33°C band. 

Model consensus and recent analogs support the narrow 32–33°C probability split, with resolution hinging on the precise timing and extent of cloud cover and any late-day convective cooling over the next 48 hours.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from models aligned with the German Weather Service show Munich's August 7 maximum stabilizing near 27–28°C after a sharp cooldown from 34°C highs on August 5. A shift to cooler maritime air, increased cloud cover, and moderate westerly flow have reduced daytime solar heating and limited further intensification. These conditions align with historical late-summer patterns following heatwaves, where temperatures typically moderate by 5–8°C within 48 hours. Market-implied odds heavily favor 28°C (63.5%) and 27°C (30.5%), consistent with the narrow consensus range in ensemble guidance and the absence of signals for renewed warming or sharp drops before sunset. Updated model runs through the afternoon will refine the final observed maximum at the reference station.

Updated model runs through the afternoon will refine the final observed maximum at the reference station.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus centers on a 92-93°F high in New York City today, reflecting model consensus for peak heating under persistent southerly flow and elevated dew points ahead of afternoon thunderstorms. Official National Weather Service guidance points to a high near 86°F with heat-index values climbing into the mid-90s, while recent runs from global ensembles and localized guidance incorporate stronger insolation and reduced cloud cover that could push Central Park or LaGuardia readings 4–6°F above the 83°F August climatological average. Key variables include the strength of the Bermuda High steering pattern and the timing of convective initiation; any delay in storm development would favor the upper end of the 90–93°F range, whereas earlier widespread showers would cap temperatures closer to 90°F. Updated NWS and NOAA model outputs this afternoon will provide the clearest signal before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency point to a maximum of 34°C in Tokyo on August 8, 2026, under partly cloudy skies with low precipitation chances.** This aligns closely with the market's clustering around 32–34°C, where traders assign roughly 94% combined probability to that narrow band. 

Typical mid-August conditions feature a strong Pacific high-pressure system promoting clear to partly cloudy weather, daytime heating, and urban heat island amplification in Tokyo that often adds 1–2°C relative to surrounding areas. The climatological normal high is 31.7°C, so current guidance reflects modestly above-average warmth consistent with the season's peak. 

Recent model runs and observations from early August (highs reaching 35–36°C) support elevated but not extreme readings, with limited downside from increased cloud cover or wind and little upside risk absent a stronger ridge or clear skies. Updated JMA guidance and ensemble spreads remain the primary near-term catalysts likely to influence further shifts in these implied probabilities.
